agent.name: KitKat Emerging Technology Landscape Agent
agent.specialty: Dated landscape intelligence, comparators, complements and decision-linked monitoring

analytical_question: P1: What current landscape options and signals matter for read-only missing-package support at a fictional US retailer?
general_et_finding: US retail decision context, dated November 17, 2026; six-month horizon. Tool-using LLM agents are offered commercially; dependable performance in sustained multi-step use varies by workflow and is not established for this case. S1 separates broad deployment status from intent; neither figure is a measurement of this exact workflow. S2 is a simulated historical evaluation and supports testing tool and policy consistency, not a current product ranking. Vendor documentation describes individual capabilities, not comparative results or availability in the specified configuration. S3 offers voluntary guidance; jurisdiction-specific obligations, current comparable cost/performance trends and relevant investment levels are unverified.
application_finding: The strongest conventional alternative is fixed order and carrier tracking lookup, a response template, and a human exception queue. Manual lookup is a fallback. A tool-selecting agent could help when scans conflict, but its relative advantage is unproven. Identity matching, timestamped fulfillment data, policy lookup, routing and reviewer capacity are necessary complements. S4 and S5 document examples of vendor capabilities rather than local connectivity.
organization_specific_finding: Stipulated setting only: the retailer compares alternatives, permits simulated read-only lookup and requires human review. Verify authorized access scope, timestamp freshness and closure ownership before relying on data. No autonomous send, loss declaration, refund, replacement or account change. No jurisdiction-specific conclusion.

evidence.claim: S1 Gartner reports 17% had deployed AI agents and more than 60% expected to deploy within two years.
evidence.source_or_reference: Gartner, The Latest Gartner Hype Cycle for Artificial Intelligence Puts Control Ahead of Capability | https://www.gartner.com/en/articles/hype-cycle-for-artificial-intelligence
evidence.evidence_type: Analyst report, broad adoption and intent
evidence.notes: Intent is not deployment. Broad self-reported status does not establish sustained production or the missing-package workflow; no comparable retailer denominator is established by the public article.

evidence.claim: S2 The benchmark evaluates multi-turn, rules- and tool-mediated agent tasks in simulated retail and airline environments.
evidence.notes: Historical task-design evidence, not live operations, current vendor ranking, or measured ROI.

evidence.claim: S3 Provides a general reference for risk identification, evaluation and oversight.
evidence.source_or_reference: NIST AI 600-1, Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile | https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.AI.600-1
evidence.notes: Not a binding local requirement, operational clearance or proof of compliance.

evidence.claim: S4 Documents fulfillment and tracking fields and scoped access options.
evidence.notes: Does not prove a specific retailer has access, fresh feed data, or audited error recovery.

evidence.claim: S5 Describes configurable routing with plan-dependent rules and options.
evidence.notes: Shows a possible workflow complement, not verified local capabilities, delivery status or performance.

evidence.claim: Fixed lookup, template and human exception queue are the stipulated comparator.
evidence.source_or_reference: KitKat Team Lab 9 internally specified P1 case
evidence.notes: Fictional access, restrictions and use case; not an operating baseline.

contrary_evidence_or_limitations: S1 does not establish comparable-population sustained use. S2 is not a live production or current head-to-head performance study.
No reviewed local permissions, deployment record, current supplier terms, market investment series or comparable operating baseline support an adoption decision.
A capable fixed workflow may already handle exceptions through routing; no matched results establish a benefit of dynamic tool selection.
confidence_and_uncertainty: Moderate confidence in the shortlist and supporting roles of documented capabilities; low confidence in relative value or local fit without a matched exception sample, access proof and measured total cost.
value_opportunity_implication: Test whether faster reconciliation of conflicting evidence offsets integration, supervision, rework and escalation effort per correctly resolved ticket.
risk_governance_implication: Track stale or conflicting scans, incorrect identification and bad escalations; confirm permitted fields and review authority with accountable owners. S3 is guidance, not permission.
recommendation_management_implication: Retain the fixed workflow as comparator and monitor the tool-selecting agent as an option. Reopen the shortlist only with comparable evidence of better exception handling without worse correctness or total cost. Hand off action to Adoption and local capacity to Organizational Adoption.
change_monitoring_triggers: P1-T1 [S1/S2 limits] Quarterly and at the decision gate: check comparable operator reports or evaluations for sustained use, correctness, escalations, and cost per correctly resolved ticket. Reopen shortlist if performance is better without worse controls or all-in cost.

P1-T2 [S4/S5] Monthly and before testing: confirm API fields, plan changes and access scope against vendor release notes and owned configuration. Reopen feasibility if required read-only data or reliable timestamps are unavailable.
P1-T3 [S3] At material policy, price or model change and before a decision: obtain owner review and current quotes. Reopen allowed scope or cost comparison as appropriate.
abstention_or_more_information_needed: Request matched exception records with approved access, baseline handling and review cost, and comparable errors/escalations.
Confirm scoped permissions, actual support policy and applicable jurisdiction with accountable reviewers. No numeric gate or vendor winner established.
